text:
WacOS

 macOS on top of Windows 11: menu bar, Dock, Finder, Spotlight, Control Center and Liquid Glass, in native C++. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 

WacOS runs on top of Windows (same kernel, drivers and apps) and replaces what you see and touch: the menu bar,
the Dock, Finder, Spotlight, Control Center, Notification Center, Mission Control, Launchpad, window title bars and a
set of built-in apps. Pick the new macOS 27 Golden Gate look, the macOS Tahoe look with Liquid Glass, the
macOS Sequoia look, or the classic Mac OS X Leopard (2007) Aqua look.

Everything is native C++ (Win32, Direct2D, DirectComposition). No Electron, no web views. It uses about 750 MB of RAM
and under 1% CPU on a 3440×1440 desktop.

 

 Contents: Screenshots · Features · Siri with AI · Install · Is it safe? ·
Roadmap · Support the project · Build · License

 Screenshots

Four themes, in System Settings Appearance Theme. Switching themes never changes your own wallpaper.

 1. macOS 27 Golden Gate (new)

The newest look, matched to Apple's macOS 27 screenshots: frosted Liquid Glass on windows, menus and the Dock,
unified toolbars, the macOS 27 icons and the Golden Gate wallpaper.

 

 
 --- --- 
 Quick Look plays video and music, with a frosted header and an animated open/close Photos with search 
 Finder System Settings Appearance, for every theme 
 Notes Calendar 
 Reminders Music with search 
 Clock with sunrise and sunset times Weather 
 Activity Monitor Preview 
 Calculator Terminal 
 TextEdit 

Also new with this theme: QuickTime Player with a frosted title bar over the video, the option to hide desktop icons,
 Edit Widgets… on the desktop menu, clicking the empty strip beside the Dock to show the desktop, Win+D handled by
the shell, grouped notifications that open on click, and smoother glass over animated wallpapers.

 Liquid Glass in motion

Real glass over whatever is behind it, live: refraction, chromatic aberration and the frost of each theme.

 

 
 --- --- 
 App switcher (Alt+Tab) Control Center 

 2. macOS Tahoe (Liquid Glass)

The macOS 26 look: clear Liquid Glass with real refraction and chromatic aberration.

 

 
 --- --- 
 Control Center in Liquid Glass, with real refraction and chromatic aberration Notification Center with widgets 
 Spotlight Applications (Spotlight's Apps mode, with categories) 
 Finder System Settings 
 Activity Monitor Force Quit Applications (Ctrl+Alt+Esc) 
 Windows message boxes become macOS alerts Dock icon styles : Default, Dark, Clear and Tinted 

 3. macOS Sequoia

The same shell with the macOS 15 look (System Settings Appearance Theme).

 

 
 --- --- 
 Control Center Notification Center 
 Launchpad Spotlight 
 Finder System Settings with the Sequoia wallpapers 

 4. Mac OS X Leopard (new)

The 2007 Aqua look, drawn from scratch (nothing reused from the modern themes): the glossy 3D Dock shelf with
reflections, the translucent menu bar, gel buttons, brushed-metal windows, Cover Flow in Finder, System Preferences
laid out like 10.5, Quick Look as a dark HUD, Dashboard, Spaces, Time Machine and the Leopard cursor (your previous cursor comes back when you switch
themes).

 

 
 --- --- 
 Finder with Cover Flow System Preferences 
 Quick Look HUD About This Mac with your PC's real specs 

 Features

- Menu bar with the active app's real menus, the Apple menu, status icons and the system tray. Hidden tray icons
 open from a list that shows each app's icon and name. New: you can move the menu bar to the bottom, beside the
 Dock (System Settings Control Center).
- Dock with magnification, running indicators, stacks (Downloads), minimized windows and the Trash. Put it on
 the bottom, left or right , hide it always or only when a window touches it ( smart hide ), and customize
 spacing, distance from the edge, corner rounding, glass color and opacity, labels, indicators and the divider.
- Change Icon… : right-click an app in the Dock or Launchpad to use your own PNG/ICO (and restore the original).
- Genie minimize animation drawn by the compositor, with smooth edges all the way into the Dock.
- Finder (file manager), Spotlight , Control Center , Notification Center , Mission Control ,
 Launchpad / Apps , Quick Look , Stage Manager and Hot Corners .
- Spotlight searches apps, files, folders and the web, does math, and completes the best match as you type, with
 Applications, Files, Actions and Clipboard modes. New: it also finds Windows settings and tools 
 ("device manager", "add or remove programs", services, display, Wi-Fi and about 200 Control Panel tasks), each
 with its own icon.
- Mac title bars (traffic lights, rounded corners, shadows) on other apps' windows, including GTK apps like
 GIMP 3. Chrome, Discord, Spotify and other Chromium/Electron apps keep their own bar but get rounded corners and a
 Mac-style border that matches the app's own light or dark look.
- Mac buttons in Chrome, Discord and other Electron apps (new, experimental , off by default): the traffic
 lights go into the app's own title bar, in place of the Windows buttons. Turn it on in System Settings Desktop &
 Dock "Mac buttons in apps with their own title bar". Feedback is welcome in the issues.
- macOS alerts in place of Windows message boxes, and the Mac Open/Save panel through Finder.
- Built-in apps : System Settings, Activity Monitor (with memory pressure), Terminal, Calculator, Notes,
 Reminders, Calendar, TextEdit, Preview, Photos, Music, QuickTime Player, Clock, Weather, Contacts,
 Time Machine, Screenshot and Force Quit.
- Siri with AI (new): ask by typing or by voice, from Spotlight, the menu bar or Win+S. Uses the AI service you
 choose with your own key, a model running on your PC, or an AI app you already have. See Siri with AI.
- Memory management like macOS : memory pressure, App Nap and purgeable memory.
- Themes : macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe, macOS Sequoia and Mac OS X Leopard.

install.title: Install
install.html:
1. Download the WacOS-<date>.zip from the latest release.
  2. Extract it anywhere and open WacOSSetup.exe: one app that installs, updates, changes and uninstalls WacOS, in the style of the macOS Installer.

The release zip includes these fonts, sounds and cursors (they aren't in the repository, and WacOSSetup.exe doesn't download them). They belong to their owners and aren't covered by the WacOS license (see License):

  • SF Pro and SF Mono, Apple's fonts (fontes folder; Apple's license applies). Installing them is optional.
  • macOS alert and interface sounds, Apple's (sons folder). They are copied along with WacOS.
  • macOS Tahoe cursor by jimmyxd2 on DeviantArt (cursor folder). Optional, and only offered with the full WacOS.
  • Mac OS X cursor, from a pack by RaZcaL inSIDe that credits Apple as the probable original author (cursor-leopard folder). It is copied along with WacOS and used by the Leopard theme.

If the fonts, alert sounds or Tahoe cursor are missing (for example, in a package you built yourself), the old instalar.cmd can offer to get them: the fonts from Apple (unpacked with 7-Zip, installed through winget if needed), 14 alert sounds from extratone/macOSsystemsounds, and the cursor from its DeviantArt page, which you download yourself.

WacOS installs for your user only (no administrator rights) in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\WacOS. Everything it changes is logged in instalacao.log there. To uninstall, use Settings > Apps > Installed apps > WacOS > Uninstall (or open WacOSSetup.exe again). The old instalar.cmd / desinstalar.cmd scripts are still in the package for advanced use.

  • Quit WacOS: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12. Emergency exit (brings Explorer back): Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F11.
Use only the apps, or only the title bars

Have your own setup? WacOSSetup.exe asks what to install:

  1. Full WacOS (menu bar, Dock, Finder...).
  2. Only the apps you pick (Finder, Notes, Calculator, Music, Preview...): shortcuts go to a WacOS folder in the Start menu. Each app draws its own Mac title bar, with or without the shell running.
  3. Only the Mac title bars on your other apps: WacOSTitleBars.exe, with an optional start at sign-in. Turn it off with WacOSTitleBars.exe --sair (it also stops when the full shell starts, which takes over).
  4. Apps + title bars.

Options 2 to 4 keep the Windows taskbar, Explorer and your folders as they are, and don't add the shell's sign-in task. Themes and language are read from System Settings (install it as one of the apps to change them). Apps that should never get the Mac title bar go one per line in %APPDATA%\Shell\janelas-excluidas.txt. The built-in apps keep the window corners Windows draws, so mods that change the corner radius (like Windhawk's rounded corners) should no longer leave a square frame around them.

features.title: Features
features.html:
• Menu bar with the active app's real menus, the Apple menu, status icons and the system tray. Hidden tray icons open from a list that shows each app's icon and name. New: you can move the menu bar to the bottom, beside the Dock (System Settings > Control Center).
  • Dock with magnification, running indicators, stacks (Downloads), minimized windows and the Trash. Put it on the bottom, left or right, hide it always or only when a window touches it (smart hide), and customize spacing, distance from the edge, corner rounding, glass color and opacity, labels, indicators and the divider.
  • Change Icon…: right-click an app in the Dock or Launchpad to use your own PNG/ICO (and restore the original).
  • Genie minimize animation drawn by the compositor, with smooth edges all the way into the Dock.
  • Finder (file manager), Spotlight, Control Center, Notification Center, Mission Control, Launchpad / Apps, Quick Look, Stage Manager and Hot Corners.
  • Spotlight searches apps, files, folders and the web, does math, and completes the best match as you type, with Applications, Files, Actions and Clipboard modes. New: it also finds Windows settings and tools ("device manager", "add or remove programs", services, display, Wi-Fi and about 200 Control Panel tasks), each with its own icon.
  • Mac title bars (traffic lights, rounded corners, shadows) on other apps' windows, including GTK apps like GIMP 3. Chrome, Discord, Spotify and other Chromium/Electron apps keep their own bar but get rounded corners and a Mac-style border that matches the app's own light or dark look.
  • Mac buttons in Chrome, Discord and other Electron apps (new, experimental, off by default): the traffic lights go into the app's own title bar, in place of the Windows buttons. Turn it on in System Settings > Desktop & Dock > "Mac buttons in apps with their own title bar". Feedback is welcome in the issues.
  • macOS alerts in place of Windows message boxes, and the Mac Open/Save panel through Finder.
  • Built-in apps: System Settings, Activity Monitor (with memory pressure), Terminal, Calculator, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, TextEdit, Preview, Photos, Music, QuickTime Player, Clock, Weather, Contacts, Time Machine, Screenshot and Force Quit.
  • Siri with AI (new): ask by typing or by voice, from Spotlight, the menu bar or Win+S. Uses the AI service you choose with your own key, a model running on your PC, or an AI app you already have. See Siri with AI.
  • Memory management like macOS: memory pressure, App Nap and purgeable memory.
  • Themes: macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe, macOS Sequoia and Mac OS X Leopard.
  • Dynamic Island (optional, System Settings > Control Center): music, timers, notifications and volume in a pill or a notch at the top of the screen, plus a clipboard history with your last 20 copies (text and files), kept across restarts and encrypted for your Windows user.
  • Game Mode like macOS: when a game comes to the front, WacOS turns off what costs the most (real glass, mouse effects, Hot Corners, file indexing) until the game quits. Game launchers (Riot Client, EA app, Ubisoft Connect, Battle.net and others) don't count as games. System Settings > Energy.
  • Launchpad: hide any app (right-click > Hide from Launchpad), or all of Windows' system tools at once.
  • Icon styles (Default, Dark, Clear, Tinted), accent colors, light and dark appearance.
  • Customize the desktop (icon size, grid spacing, text size, widgets), notifications (banner duration, Notification Center widgets) and the menu bar (show it on every display or only the main one).
  • Calendar with your country's holidays and Monday/Sunday start, Weather with any city as your location, Clock with custom cities and alarms.
  • 12 languages: English (default), Portuguese, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Russian, Polish and Turkish (System Settings > General > Language). Dates follow the language too.
